headline: Wall Street Eyes a Shaky Open After Friday's Chip-Led Rout
body_html:
Markets in the Asia-Pacific region are pointing lower ahead of the New York open. Australian shares are set to slide at the start of trade and New Zealand is already falling, according to Reuters. That follows a punishing Friday, November 20, when 558 of the 666 stocks we track fell and only 102 rose.

The dollar has edged back from a 19-month high after the rout, while the yen softens. Oil is holding a tight range as Gulf attacks keep a risk premium in prices, and the Houthis say they struck a Saudi refinery. With intraday prices not yet meaningful, the open will turn on whether Friday's selling in chips carries over.

Semiconductors fell 10.02% on Friday, the worst sector by a wide margin. Applied Optoelectronics lost 16.55%, Sandisk 16.05%, Celestica 16.00%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 15.32% and Credo Technology 15.2%. Bloom Energy slid 15.3%. Financials lost 3.53% and energy 3.33%. Homebuilders, up 0.32%, were the only sector in the green, and apparel names such as Gap, up 11.44%, held firm.

briefs.headline: Asia-Pacific Sets a Soft Tone
briefs.body: Australian shares are expected to open lower and New Zealand is already in the red, Reuters reports. The regional weakness extends the cautious mood left by Friday's heavy selling in the US. Traders will watch whether Monday's open in New York follows that lead or finds buyers.

briefs.headline: Dollar Pulls Back From Its Peak
briefs.body: The dollar has edged off a 19-month high after last week's market rout, while the yen softens. Currency moves have become a useful gauge of risk appetite. A further retreat could ease pressure on markets, but a rebound would hint at lingering caution.

briefs.headline: Gulf Attacks Keep Oil on Edge
briefs.body: Oil is trading in a tight range as attacks in the Gulf sustain a risk premium. The Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery. Energy shares fell 3.33% on Friday, so crude's reaction at the open will be closely watched.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Take the Brunt of Friday's Fall
briefs.body: Semiconductors dropped 10.02% on Friday, far worse than any other group. Sandisk fell 16.05%, Credo Technology 15.2% and Alpha and Omega Semiconductor 15.32%. Optical and server-hardware names also sank. Whether the selling continues or steadies is the main question for the open.

briefs.headline: Apparel Retailers Buck the Trend
briefs.body: In a market where 558 of 666 stocks fell, clothing retailers stood out. Gap rose 11.44% and The Buckle gained 5.67%, topping Friday's leaderboard. Spectrum Brands added 6.3%. Homebuilders, up 0.32%, were the only sector to finish higher.

briefs.headline: Officials Warn of More Tech Outages
briefs.body: The US intelligence chief expects more technology outages as systems are upgraded, warning of bumps in the road. Separately, Delta flights saw brief delays at Atlanta's airport because of an automated-system problem. Reliability of critical systems remains a theme to watch.
